title: Tiny Pond Creature Breaks Usual DNA "Stop" Rules
summary:
Scientists testing a DNA tool found a surprise in a tiny pond creature. In most living things, certain DNA signals tell a cell to stop building a protein. In this protist, those "stop" signals instead code for two different amino acids—the building blocks of proteins.

Dr. Jamie McGowan studied the organism from a freshwater pond at Oxford University Parks in England. The team was not hunting for weird codes. They were testing a way to read DNA from very small samples. When they looked at the genome, the rules looked different.

The protist is called Oligohymenophorea sp. PL0344. Findings in PLOS Genetics showed the genetic code can be more flexible than many people thought. Later work found more odd codes in related microbes.

Protists are living things with cell nuclei that are not animals, plants, or fungi. McGowan said it was lucky they picked this one—and it shows how much is still unknown.
why_it_matters: Science surprises remind kids that nature still has mysteries to discover.
